messages:
Priya: quick flag FYI 10: we rolled a kernel-preference change targeting 'micro-kernel' for short requests (<50 tokens) and we're seeing p99 jumps on canaries.
Ben: ouch. p99 how big?
Priya: baseline p99 ~210ms -> now ~320ms on canary hosts. p50 flat. so tail only.
Carlos: tail + short requests usually means host-side jitter or kvcache hash collisions. any flamegraphs?
Priya: grabbed a few; top lines aggregated by category: 
```
host ingress samples:
- parse/tokenize: 28%
- kvcache lookup + lock: 26%
- grpc small-write stalls: 18%
- kernel selection pathing: 12%
- syscall overhead: 9%
- other: 7%
```
Jin: kvcache + tokenize together ~54% 1looks bad. Did kernel change alter request routing that increases hot keys per shard?
Priya: yes, the micro-kernel routing pins requests to fewer host threads to keep latency predictable. that increases local kvcache pressure.
Ben: so it's an interaction: kernel selector reduces GPU time but increases kvcache contention -> tail latency.
Carlos: options: 1) relax pinning so requests spread across shards, 2) change kvcache sharding (add secondary hash), 3) move tokenize earlier to edge to amortize work, 4) add a fastpath for tiny requests bypassing kvcache.
Jin: adding a secondary hash (xor with seq id) reduced collisions in my unit test. low risk change.
Priya: note: bypassing kvcache for tiny requests is attractive because miss penalty is small and saves lock contention. but we lose some reuse for short dialogues.
Ben: what about batching heuristics? if we increase host-side batching threshold by 1-2 requests we might reduce per-request syscalls and smooth writes. Could help p99.
Carlos: true, but batching increases queuing latency for p50. need a selective policy: only batch when seq_len < 40 and parallelism low.
Priya: perf-bot ran patch tryjobs overnight: patch that relaxed affinity and added secondary hash shows p99 down to 235ms (canary), still above baseline but much better.
perf-bot: tryjob 1795567002 results: canary p99=235ms, p50=46ms, baseline p99=210ms. diff: -26% vs previous canary, +12% vs baseline.
Jin: I'll open PR for secondary-hash + metrics to surface kvcache lock hold time.
Ben: I'll prototype a token-buffer pool for ingress (reuse arrays) and add a benchmark. cut allocations -> less GC/alloc stalls.
Carlos: also suggest enabling grpc write coalescing in the sidecar for 72h A/B. lowers syscall count; we measured 30% fewer write() calls locally.
Priya: agreed. plan: (A) land secondary-hash + affinity relaxation to canary (B) Jin adds kvcache lock histograms + dashboards (C) Ben lands tokenizer buffer pool PR with microbench (D) Carlos flips sidecar coalesce behind flag.
Jin: will include a canary job that records kvcache contention percentiles.
Carlos: tagging @infra-sre to monitor host CPU spin.
Priya: thanks all. if canary looks good we'll roll to prod next week, otherwise we revert kernel preference and iterate. :rocket:
